entities.summary:
Charles du Plessis d'Argentré (1673-05-16, Argentré-du-Plessis - 1740-10-17) was a French Catholic theologian and bishop of Tulle, whose influential treatises on spirituality and ecclesiastical governance helped shape the Counter-Reformation efforts in 18th-century France.

 As a prominent theologian, d'Argentré contributed to the development of Jansenist thought, a movement that emphasized devotion, asceticism, and the importance of the role of the Church in society. His work, in turn, influenced the intellectual and religious landscape of Western Europe during the Enlightenment period.

 The legacy of d'Argentré can be seen in the continued relevance of his treatises on spirituality and ecclesiastical governance, which remain studied by scholars and theologians today.

 'The best way to understand the Church is to love it,' d'Argentré once said, a testament to his enduring impact on the Catholic Church and its followers.
